text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Aston Villa and Tottenham at Villa Park.
Villa went through a rocky patch in the Premier League and only won one of their first four matches in 2024, disrupting their charge towards qualification for next season's Champions League.
However, the Lions have improved their form and have won three successive games in the top flight.
After triumphs over Fulham and Nottingham Forest, it looked like Villa were easing their way to another victory when they were 2-0 ahead at half-time.
Yet, second-half strikes from Tahith Chong and Carlton Morris for the Hatters set up an enthralling finish.
Despite Luton's impressive comeback to level the score, Unai Emery's side prevailed thanks to Lucas Digne, who netted an 89th-minute winner for Villa.
The hosts are five points above fifth-place Tottenham, so they will strengthen their grip on a place in fourth if they can beat a direct rival.
Although, Villa might be slightly more tired than their opponents after travelling to Ajax for a 0-0 draw in the first leg of their Europa Conference League last-16 tie in midweek.

Spurs have only lost one of their last seven Premier League matches, but there are still plenty of things to improve for Ange Postecoglou's men if they want to stand a chance of finishing in the top four this campaign.
The visitors haven't won back-to-back matches in the top flight since December (where they won three in a row) and haven't kept a clean sheet in their last nine games.
Additionally, the Lilywhites have conceded first in their previous four league outings but came from behind to beat a spirited Crystal Palace side in their last fixture.
Eberechi Eze opened the scoring for the Eagles with a sublime second-half free-kick before Tottenham turned it around with goals from Timo Werner, Cristian Romero and Son Heung-min.

If Spurs can win for just the second time in seven matches on the road in the Premier League, they will go two points behind Villa and have control of their destiny due to having a game in hand on their opponents.
Villa make three changes to the side that drew 0-0 with Ajax in the first leg of their Europa Conference League last-16 match against Ajax.
Captain McGinn regains his place in the side and replaces 20-year-old Iroegbunam.
Bailey starts ahead of Diaby on the wing, with Cash also picked ahead of Rogers.
Tottenham make three alterations to the team that beat Palace 3-1 in their previous Premier League outing.
Porro is back after missing the last two matches with a muscle injury and appears at right-back instead of Royal.
Sarr replaces Bentancur in the midfield, with the final change coming in the attack.
Werner scored his first goal for Spurs against the Eagles but is out of the side for Johnson, who registered two assists against Palace.
Villa have won their last three Premier League meetings with Tottenham, their longest league winning run over Spurs since January 1996 (a run of four).
Both teams are on the pitch and are ready to get started.
Tottenham get this Premier League clash under way.
A win for Villa would strengthen their grip on fourth position and a guaranteed place in the Champions League next season.
However, a triumph for Spurs would put them in control of their own fate.
United aren’t even playing today, but they will be watching this contest keenly after beating Everton 2-0 yesterday.
The Red Devils are eight points behind Villa, so are still in the race for a place in next season’s Champions League.
Erik ten Hag will probably be hoping for a draw.
There is a very loud atmosphere around Villa Park, with the hosts desperate for a win.
Emery's men have had most of the possession in the early exchanges but haven't been able to do anything with it and are just trying to build their way into the match.
Spurs are looking to play a high press.
TACKLE! What an important intervention from Van De Ven! A long ball out of the Villa defence is flicked on by Watkins, who runs around Romero and into the box.
He tries to get a shot away on his right foot, but Van de Ven gets back brilliantly to make a strong tackle.
Watkins stays down, but he will be fine to continue.
Spurs play the ball around patiently in Villa's half, switching it from left to right before Kulusevski takes control on the touchline.
He rolls a pass through to Porro, but the right-back sends his cross straight out for a goal-kick.
Villa demand that the flag goes up for offside against the Spaniard, but nothing is given.
McGinn receives a pass out of the defence and is immediately put under pressure by Bissouma, who gets in quickly to win the ball before giving away a free-kick.
That was lucky for Villa, as the foul was very soft.
Spurs would have had a clear chance to score.
Udogie bursts down the left and flashes a brilliant cross just in front of Martinez, but Kulusevski cannot get there quickly enough to tap the ball in from close range.
The Sweden international collects it on the right and sends another cross into the box, but the Villa defence clear it away.
Romero has possession on the left in Spurs' half, taking a long time on the ball before passing it into the midfield.
Watkins shows his frustrations and makes a late tackle on the defender.
The England international still looks hurt from the early tackle from Van de Ven.
Villa haven’t been able to impose themselves on the contest and are giving possession away cheaply.
Martinez keeps attempting to play a long ball over the top to Watkins, but the striker cannot hold it up and is being nullified by the Spurs defence.
He has only had three touches.
Bissouma plays a pass straight to Wakins in Spurs' defensive third, with the forward rolling a pass down the left to Tielemans.
However, his shot is blocked.
Villa retain possession, but a lofted switch over to Cash down the right has too much pace on it, with the ball going behind for a goal-kick.
It’s taken 15 minutes for the first shot.
Son will be the player to watch for Spurs today.
Since the start of the 2020-21 campaign, only Mohamed Salah (118) and Harry Kane (96) have more goals and assists combined in the Premier League than Spurs’ captain (63 goals and 29 assists).

Son also has five goals in three appearances at Villa Park (one every 52 minutes); among players to play 250 or more minutes at a Premier League stadium, only Luis Suarez at Carrow Road (one every 38 minutes) has a better minutes to goal ratio than Son at Villa Park.
He has been crowded out so far, but the South Korea international only needs a second to create magic for the visitors.
Cash gives away a free-kick on the left in a crossing position.
However, Porro's inswinging cross is headed away by Lenglet.
Villa break away on the counter through McGinn, who finds Luiz, The Brazilian threads a throughball to Wakins, but he is just offside.
Sarr is the first player to go into the book after a tangle of legs with Bailey.
McGinn is over the following free-kick on the right and curls a cross into the box, but Vicario takes command of the situation and punches it away.
He should have caught it, but didn’t want to take any risks.
Villa are putting the ball into the box on every occasion, with Cash taking long throws from the right.
The Tottenham defence clear the initial danger before Bailey's left-footed strike from the edge is blocked.
Luiz was ready to have a shot just behind him, but it was taken away from his toes.
Villa are having a dominant spell and are putting Spurs under pressure.
Udogie does well to intercept a pass down the right to Cash, but the hosts keep possession through McGinn, who switches the play over to Digne on the left.
The Frenchman then looks to put a cross into the box, but it is caught by Vicario.
Luiz and Maddison get into a confrontation off the ball, with the Villa man raising his hands in the air indicating that he has nothing to do with the situation.
Referee Chris Kavanagh calls them over for a chat to cool things down.
That will be something to watch for the rest of the contest.

Tottenham have scored in all 26 Premier League matches under Postecoglou so far, the best run of scoring from a manager’s first game in the English top-flight since Arthur Rowe at Spurs in the 1950-51 season when they won the title (scored in the first 27 games).
The visitors will want to extend that run, but they will have to get a shot away first.
Spurs have had 64.9 per cent of the possession, but nothing to show for it.
WIDE! Cash goes close! Wakins holds onto the ball brilliantly and waits for support.
He finds Cash, who slides a pass to Bailey on the byline.
The winger then cuts the ball back to Cash, but he pokes his effort wide of the right post after a scramble.
Tottenham are putting Villa under plenty of pressure.
Martinez plays a short pass to Konza, who is lucky to escape Johnson after his clearance flicks off the winger and goes forward.
However, Johnson doesn’t give up on the challenge, forcing him back to the corner flag before blocking his clearance again.
Bailey is playing up front next to Watkins.
However, he is struggling to get involved.
He has only had 13 touches, completing only one of his five passes so far.
PENALTY SHOUT! Cash wins possession off Maddison and allows his side to stream forward on the attack.
He finds Watkins, who rolls a pass through to Bailey, but he is tackled by Bissouma inside the box.
The Villa man wants a penalty, but Bissouma gets a touch on the ball.
Udogie drives inside from the left and attempts to poke a pass through to Son, but his ball into the South Korean is blocked.
He tries to rescue the Spurs attack by wresting with Konza to regain possession, but he throws him to the floor and gifts a free-kick to the hosts.
Another nearly moment that comes to nothing for Spurs.
This is the latest into a Premier League game that Spurs have gone without a shot this season, with their previous-longest being a 20th-minute attempt against Brighton in February.
This has been far from a classic, with Villa only having three shots worth an xG (expected goals) of 0.31.
So few chances or moments of quality from either side shows how much this contest means in the battle for a spot in the top four and a place in next season's Champions League.
Neither team wants to give anything away easily.
Johnson looks to create something for Spurs, driving down the left before drilling a cross-shot towards the near post.
However, Martínez is aware of the danger and collects it easily.
Son threads a pass down the left side of the box to Johnson, who is put under pressure by a crowd but can poke a cutback into the middle.
However, nobody is there to tap it in, allowing Villa to clear it away.
CHANCE! Romero is loose in possession, and Bailey gets in quickly to win the ball.
He offloads a pass to Watkins, who gets down the left side of the box.
He has an opportunity to get a shot away on his left foot but cuts onto his right and has his attempt blocked by Romero.
The hosts have a corner moments later and take it short to McGinn, but his cross is directed just wide by Digne.
HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 0-0 TOTTENHAM
Villa and Tottenham struggled to create any meaningful attacking chances in a first half that ended goalless.
The hosts had five shots but failed to test Vicario in the Spurs net.
Watkins had an early opportunity on the right side of the box after flicking the ball past Romero.
However, Van de Ven got back brilliantly to stop the striker from getting a shot away.
Tielemans, Watkins and Bailey had attempts blocked, with Cash poking a shot wide of the right post and Digne shouldering an effort across the goal and off target with the final attack of the half.
Tottenham lacked any threat going forward, with Johnson's effort from a tight angle going straight at Martinez in what was their only shot of the half.
Rarely a team that created an xG of 0.48 with five shots and zero on target would be better than their opponents going into half-time, but that’s the case for Villa against Tottenham.
The hosts have looked threatening at times on the counter through Watkins and Bailey, but the Lions have not been able to get their forward involved enough.
The pair combined for just 32 touches before the break.
As for Spurs, they only had one attempt, worthy of an xG of only 0.03.
The visitors have only had 10 touches inside the opposition box, with Johnson accounting for six of them.
Son has been crowded out by the three Villa centre-backs and will be hoping to be more involved after the restart.
Villa get the ball rolling again.
No changes at the break.
Cash makes any early drive down the right and has Watkins ready for a cross in the middle of the box.
The right-back goes alone, cutting inside before having a left-footed shot blocked in the box.
Watkins is furious and has his hands in the air.
OFFSIDE! Fast start to the second half from Villa.
Digne plays the inside to Torres, who plays a reverse pass through to Bailey.
He runs from right to left to get onto it, but he strikes his effort over before the flag goes up.
Van de Ven goes down off the ball and looks like he is in some discomfort.
He cannot continue and will be replaced.
Van de Ven is forced off with an injury and is replaced by Dragusin, who signed from Genoa in January.
This is his fourth appearance off the bench, but the earliest he has come on.
GOALLLL! MADDISON SCORES! 1-0 SPURS! What a goal that could be in the race for Champions League qualification.
Porro combines with Kulusevski in Tottenham's half, and he threads a pass down the right to Sarr.
He rushes forward and curls a brilliant cross into Maddison, who bundles it in from close range.
What an assist from Sarr.
He makes a brilliant run to get down the right, but his cross is even better.
He flashes it into Maddison, who simply has to poke it in from close range.
Maddison has been directly involved in nine goals across his eight away Premier League appearances for Spurs (three goals and six assists).
He’s also scored in two of his last four appearances at Villa Park (three goals).
GOALLL! JOHNSON SCORES! 2-0 SPURS! The visitors have netted twice in quick succession.
Konsa is loose in possession and is tackled by Kulusevski, who plays a short pass to Son.
He has options on either side but finds Johnson to his left, with the Wales international crashing his effort into the roof of the net.
Son is smart.
He has to decide where to play the ball on the edge of the box, slotting it over to Johnson on his left, with the forward free.
There is still plenty to do for Johnson, but he finishes the chance emphatically.
Son has had a hand in 10 goals across his last nine away Premier League appearances (seven goals and three assists).
Tottenham looked lost in the attack in the first half and only had one shot, but have been superb since the restart.
Villa are looking tired, which could be because of their away trip to Ajax in the Europa Conference League in midweek.
Emery has seen enough and has decided to make three changes.
He is going for a more attacking side, with Lenglet coming off for Zaniolo.
Tielemans has only had 20 touches and is off for Diaby.
This is his sixth consecutive appearance off the bench.
The Frenchman registered an important assist against Luton in Villa’s last match.
There is also a straight swap on the left for Villa.
Moreno will bring a fresh pair of legs as he replaces Digne.
Son gets behind Cash on the left and swings an inviting cross into the heart of the box.
However, it is just too far ahead of Kulusevski, who cannot get there.
Villa need to do something to turn the momentum in their favour.
Dragusin stops Villa from taking a quick free-kick and goes into the book.
Spurs have another chance to score.
Johnson receives the ball on the touchline around the halfway line and drives a first-time pass through to Udogie, but he puts too much on it, and Martinez claims.
CHANCE! Diaby does brilliantly to win the ball back in Spurs' defensive third and finds McGinn, who gets to the byline before drilling a low cross into the box.
Zaniolo is there, but Porro and Vicario work together to clear it away.
RED CARD! Villa are down to 10 men after a horrendous tackle from McGinn.
Udogie skips past him, and the Lions captain lunges across him without trying to win the ball.
It’s a naughty challenge, and the Spurs players are quite rightly furious.
Udogie gets up from the tackle before going back down again.
He needs medical treatment but will be able to continue.
A difficult comeback for Villa might have just become impossible.
McGinn has received his first red card in 205 league appearances in English football.
There was really no question about it.
Villa make another switch.
Bailey has been largely ineffective and has completed just 36.4 per cent of his passes.
Iroegbunam is on.
Sarr got a brilliant assist for Spurs' first goal and is now being given a rest after an energetic performance in the midfield.
Bentancur is on.
Zaniolo uses his quick feet and speed to drive forward with possession, skipping a couple of tackles before switching the ball over to Diaby on the right.
However, he cannot take control of it, allowing Udogie to get across and thump it clear.
CHANCE! Spurs waste a scoring chance.
The visitors win possession high up the pitch again, with Son dribbling forward before rolling a pass through to Kulusevski on the right side of the box.
He could shoot but goes back to Son, who is crowded out, before having his pass intercepted.
OVER! Bentancur collects the ball in space in the middle of Spurs' half and surges forward before rolling a pass out to Kulusevski.
He gets to the edge of Villa's box, cutting inside before lifting his effort well over the bar.
Son was free to his left and is annoyed that he didn’t get the ball.
Villa have only had three shots in the second half (zero on target worth an xG of 0.17).
Their performance is summed up in a corner from Luiz, who sends a low cross straight to Porro at the front post.
Luiz looks for options just inside Spurs' half, lofting a pass over the top of the defence and through to Diaby down the right.
He doesn’t look at the options in the box, cutting the ball back to the edge, where nobody is there.
This has been a worrying performance from the hosts.
Maddison receives the ball in Villa's half and threads an over-hit throughball to Kulusevski.
He keeps the attack alive on the byline and lifts a cross over to Johnson, but his shot is blocked at close range.
Villa Park has gone quiet, they have had nothing to cheer about.
Porro is in plenty of space on the right and is given the time to whip a low cross into the heart of the box.
Son darts inside to try and get a shot away, but Cash sticks to his man and helps the ball onto Martinez.

Tottenham have only won one of their last six away Premier League games (drawing three and losing two) despite scoring two or more goals in five of those games, all of which have been in their last five trips.
Before today, Spurs last scored two or more goals in six away league games in a row between May and September 2017.
This time, they will probably be getting a deserved win for their efforts.
SAVE! An important stop from Vicario.
Luiz's outswinging cross from the right is headed on to Zaniolo, whose effort from close range at the back post is bravely blocked by Vicario.
The Italian lands on the goalkeeper, who looks hurt and needs treatment.
Villa make their final change.
Carlos returns from injury and replaces Konza at centre-back.
Vicario is back on his feet and is in goal to defend a Villa corner that comes to nothing.
He will be desperate to keep a clean sheet for the first time in 10 outings.
Tottenham are making two changes.
Maddison is given a warm reception from the away fans after scoring Spurs' first goal and is replaced by Werner, who will not give the Villa defence a moment of rest.
Johnson scored Spurs' second goal that put the contest beyond Villa and probably started the hosts to get frustrated.
Hojbjerg is on to help the away side see out the match.
Hojbjerg fakes his way beyond two Villa players before slotting the ball through to Son on the right.
His low cross is cleared as far as Kulusevski, who has his shot from close range tackled behind by Carlos.
It looked like he was going to get a goal that his performance has deserved.
GOALLLLL! SON SCORES! 3-0 SPURS! Tottenham make a statement at Villa Park.
Porro and Kulusevski combine with a clever one-two in a tight space on the right, with the Sweden international breaking free before cutting the ball across to Son.
The captain is free in the middle, and he smashes his strike into the roof of the net.

events.action: smashes his strike into the roof of the net

text: Kulusevski could have scored just moments ago, but he gets an assist to his name.
He works well with Porro in a tight space, breaking free of a couple of markers before finding Son, who does the rest.
There will be 10 minutes of additional time.

GOALLL! WERNER SCORES! 4-0 SPURS! Son skips down the left side of the box and pushes the ball past Cash before squaring a pass across to Werner, who sends a first-time finish across the goal and into the right corner.
One goal and two assists for Son.
He is too quick and clever for Cash, using his speed to get past the right-back before getting his head up to find Werner.
It's an instinctive finish from the forward, who scores for the second consecutive match.
That is Werner's first Premier League strike against Villa on his fourth appearance against them in the competition.
That will give him great confidence.
Son tries to make a run around Carlos to get the ball but speeds straight into the Villa defender and goes to the floor.
There was absolutely nothing in that, with the Spurs man making the most of it.
FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 0-4 TOTTENHAM
Tottenham scored four goals in a dominant second-half display to beat Villa 4-0 at Villa Park and put qualification for next season's Champions League in their hands.
Spurs only created an xG of 0.03 before the break but were a completely different side after the restart.
Maddison poked in Sarr's cross to put the visitors ahead, with Johnson crashing his strike into the roof of the net just 207 seconds later to put Postecoglou's men in control.
Things went from bad to worse for Villa when McGinn got sent off for a horrendous tackle on Udogie and took 84 minutes to have their first attempt on target.
Spurs were ruthless and scored twice in stoppage time.
Son hammered his effort from inside the box past Martinez before assisting Werner moments later for his second goal in two outings.
Spurs are just two points behind fourth-placed Villa and have played one fewer match.
They travel to Fulham next week looking for their third straight win.
As for Villa, they have conceded two or more goals in three successive games and host Ajax in the second leg of their Europa Conference League last-16 tie.
That's all for today, goodbye.
